chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad, from al-Husayn, from al-Nadr, from Hisham, from Sulayman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no alms-tax (zakat) in the dates until they amount to five awsiq, and the same applies to grapes until they amount to five awsiq of raisins.

key_terms.أَوْسَاقٍ: Awiq (plural of wasq, a unit of volume/weight)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of dates or grapes required to incur zakat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the nisab for zakat on agricultural produce, establishing five awsiq as the threshold for both dates and dried grapes (zabib). It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on measuring the net yield after drying, ensuring fairness in the obligation of alms on natural resources.
